newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya shilling eases on new dollar demand.
newsitem.headline: Kenya shilling eases on new dollar demand.

text.p: The Kenyan shilling weakened marginally against the dollar on Monday as dollar buying interest picked up, commercial bank dealers said.
The central bank of Kenya posted a mean shilling average of 54.66 from 54.64 on Friday against the dollar while against the pound it was posted at 90.97 from 91.76 on Friday.
"We have seen some dollar demand from the power and manufacturing sectors," one dealer said.
"But this demand is not likely to weaken the shilling in a permanent way. A lot of it is from investors who've carried forward last year's bills not because of strategic buying," another dealer said.
The money market tightened with overnight rates quoted as high as 25 percent.
"Most banks are anticipating paying for maturing treasury bills and taxes from Tuesday," one dealer said. "Add on to that the fact that the market was already illiquid," he added.
